reasons: Claimed status is compliant and the cited text supports it: Section 14 (p0079) gives Client an unconditional at-will termination right on written notice, with service ceasing at the end of the month following the notice month (~30–60 days), which meets the preferred/fallback notice window, and no early-termination fee, penalty or liquidated damages appears in the cited paragraphs.

Vendor has no mid-term convenience exit: Section 13 (p0078) fixes a one-year term with auto-renewal, and TrueLink's only unilateral cut-off of Sections 2 and 3 is cause-based (Client breach / breach of Sections 8a–8c), so the walk-away trigger (Vendor convenience termination on <90 days) does not arise mid-term.
The 12-month term also defeats the 'no Customer convenience right in a multi-year term' walk-away, and Client in any event has a convenience right.

Shortfalls are correctly treated as minor sub-elements noted rather than redlined: no express pro-rata refund (largely moot because p0045 bills monthly in arrears) and a mutual 30-day non-renewal notice that operates only at natural expiry and equally preserves our own flexibility — flagging it would cut against our party.

Consistent with a compliant finding, no redline and no counterparty comment were proposed; the failed 'Customer convenience termination present' regex is a phrasing artifact (Section 14 expresses the right as continued service until Client's elected termination date) rather than a substantive gap.
The open cross-reference to the unreviewed Section 4 is appropriately surfaced as a confirmation item rather than asserted as a breach.
